evidence.quote: The calibrated data were retrieved using the script for PI provided by the observatory. In order to improve the SNR, the data were self-calibrated, in each EB separately.
The data were calibrated by the NAASC, and two rounds of phase-only self-calibration were applied to each set of observations.
J0510+1800 was used as flux, bandpass, pointing, and atmosphere calibrator, while J0440+1437 and J0438+3004 were used as phase calibrators.

evidence.quote: In each EB we applied from one to four rounds of phase-only self-calibration, stopping the calibration when no significant improvement was measured in the SNR from one step to the next one.
We then concatenated all EBs and applied one round of amplitude self-calibration.
As final step, we have applied the phase and amplitude calibration to the spectral windows containing emission lines.

analysis_steps.goal: Measure total fluxes and gas and dust disc radii (R68 and R95)

method.value: Apply the cumulative flux (curve of growth) aperture photometry technique on 12CO, 13CO, C18O zeroth moment maps and continuum images using concentric elliptical annuli (or rectangular apertures for HK Tau B, half-disc masks for DH Tau A and UZ Tau Wa/Wb, and imfit-constrained total flux for RW Aur A/B)

evidence.loc: Disc radii estimate: the cumulative flux technique
evidence.quote: Once the maximum flux is calculated, we estimate the disc radius $R_\mathrm{disc}$ (or $R_{95}$) as the radius containing $95\%$ of the total flux and the effective disc radius $R_\mathrm{eff}$ (or $R_{68}$) as that containing $68\%$ of the total flux.

evidence.loc: Disc radii estimate: the cumulative flux technique
evidence.quote: The uncertainty on the radius is calculated considering the statistical error on the maximum flux and, since the error in the radius estimate must be at least half of the resolution, we summed in quadrature this error with 0.075$''$.

findings_qualitative.value: Observed 95% gas disc radii are typically 0.15-0.35 times the projected separation, yielding minimum orbital eccentricities of ~0.15-0.5 (average ~0.3), consistent with main-sequence binary eccentricities without requiring highly eccentric (e > 0.7) orbits.

findings_qualitative.value: Most binaries where both components are resolved (RW Aur, DK Tau, HK Tau) are misaligned (relative inclinations ~25 deg to ~50 deg), while UZ Tau discs are better aligned (<= 0-20 deg), suggesting formation via turbulent fragmentation.

evidence.quote: The discs in the UZ Tau system show relative inclination differences $\lesssim 0-20 \si{\ensuremath{^\circ}}$, while the RW Aur, DK Tau and HK Tau systems show a larger relative inclination ($\sim 25 \si{\ensuremath{^\circ}}$, $\sim 40 \si{\ensuremath{^\circ}}$, and $\sim 50 \si{\ensuremath{^\circ}}$, respectively).
We conclude that most of the observed binaries appear not to be coplanar, possibly a result of turbulent fragmentation, rather than disc fragmentation.

claims.hypothesis: Gas disc radii in multiple stellar systems are larger than dust disc radii by factors of ~2-3, reconciling small observed dust disc radii with tidal truncation models without invoking extremely high orbital eccentricities (e > 0.7).
claims.experiment: Measured 12CO gas disc radii (R68 and R95) using the cumulative flux technique on high-resolution ALMA Band 6 data for 8 multiple systems in Taurus and compared them with Galario dust radii and Artymowicz & Lubow (1994) analytical tidal truncation models.
claims.result: Gas disc radii are ~2-4 times larger than dust radii; R95,gas/a_p is typically ~0.15-0.35 (> 0.1 in all targets), yielding minimum orbital eccentricities of ~0.15-0.5 (average ~0.3).
claims.finding: Tidal truncation models explain the observed gas disc sizes in multiple systems with moderate eccentricities (~0.15-0.5) consistent with main-sequence low-mass binaries, confirming that highly eccentric orbits are not required.

why_this_data.value: Longer integration time (~40 min/source) in ALMA Band 6 at ~0.15'' resolution was needed on the Manara et al. (2019) multiple-system sample to detect CO molecular emission lines with high SNR and measure gas disc sizes.

evidence.quote: Our aim is to test tidal truncation models by measuring for the first time the gas size of discs in multiple stellar systems in a uniform way, with the same instrument and a similar noise level at high spatial resolution.
In fact, the aim of the new observations was to detect different molecular emission lines with a higher signal-to-noise (SNR).

why_this_method.value: The cumulative flux technique on zeroth moment maps captures the outer gas disc extent where emission is faint without assuming a parametric profile, while Galario uv-plane dust radii from Manara et al. (2019) achieve sub-beam resolution and enable direct comparison with Sanchis et al. (2021).

evidence.loc: Disc radii estimate: the cumulative flux technique
evidence.quote: As shown by the red solid ellipses, the radii estimated with the cumulative flux technique get the really outer extent of the discs, where little emission is detected, giving the possibility to test tidal truncation models.

evidence.loc: Comparing dust and gas disc radii
evidence.quote: For the following discussion, we use the values of $R_\mathrm{dust}$ obtained by (cite: 2019Manara+) by modelling the continuum data in the visibility plane using the *Galario* library (cite: 2018Tazzari+) because this makes the results directly comparable with (cite: 2021Sanchis+), who performed a similar analysis.

evidence.loc: Comparison between new continuum data and older continuum data
evidence.quote: Since in the visibility plane analysis a resolution under the beam size is achievable, the dust radii estimated using *Galario* are more reliable, especially for the more compact discs.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Fitting HK Tau B with eddy and measuring its gas radius with elliptical annuli; rejected because HK Tau B is edge-on and vertically extended, so rectangular apertures along the major axis and literature PA/inclination were used instead.

evidence.loc: Geometrical properties of discs from Keplerian modeling
evidence.quote: We did not fit the disc around the secondary star of the HK Tau system. This disc is almost edge-on, so that the assumption of geometrically thin disc emission cannot be applied and the vertical height of the disc must be considered.

evidence.loc: Disc radii estimate: the cumulative flux technique
evidence.quote: To correct for this effect, the disc radius is measured along the major axis, centering on the source rectangles with increasing width and fixed height

how_they_decided_enough.value: Stopped phase-only self-calibration rounds when no significant SNR improvement occurred from one step to the next; ran eddy MCMC chains for ~1000-2000 steps with 200 walkers until convergence.

evidence.quote: In each EB we applied from one to four rounds of phase-only self-calibration, stopping the calibration when no significant improvement was measured in the SNR from one step to the next one.

evidence.loc: Geometrical properties of discs from Keplerian modeling
evidence.quote: The number of walkers and steps needed to achieve the convergence of the chain were typically $200$ walkers and $\sim1000$-$2000$ steps, with the last $\sim800$-$1000$ steps used to sample the posterior distribution.

limitations_admitted.value: Only the C43-6 configuration was executed (C43-3 was not executed), limiting the maximum recoverable scale to ~1.8''.

evidence.quote: Two configurations were requested, C43-6 and C43-3, but only observations in the former configuration were executed. Therefore, the maximum recoverable scale of the observations was only $\sim$1.8$^{\prime\prime}$.

limitations_admitted.value: Foreground cloud absorption affects 12CO emission near systemic or redshifted velocities in almost all discs, particularly DH Tau A where the southern half is totally absorbed.

evidence.quote: Signatures of partial absorption around the systemic velocity is observed in almost all discs; absorption in the red-shifted velocities is observed in the disc around CIDA 9 A, while the red-shifted velocities around DH Tau A are totally absorbed by the cloud below the continuum level.

limitations_admitted.value: T Tau and UY Aur do not show Keplerian rotation patterns and could not be analysed for individual disc radii.

evidence.quote: Finally, the observation of UY Aur and T Tau do not show a velocity pattern compatible with Keplerian rotation (see Section 3), making it difficult to determine if the gas emission is reflecting the disc dynamics, and therefore to estimate the radius of individual discs.

limitations_admitted.value: Analytical co-planar face-on tidal truncation models cannot explain the large R95,gas/a_p values in CIDA 9 A, UZ Tau, and RW Aur without high orbital inclination or additional physical processes (substructures, tidal interactions).

evidence.loc: Comparison of gas disc radii with tidal truncation models
evidence.quote: The tidal truncation models assuming face-on inclination of the orbit cannot explain the observed large values of $R_\mathrm{t}/a_\mathrm{p}$ in the CIDA 9, UZ Tau, and RW Aur systems, except assuming unrealistic parameters ($e\sim 1$ and targets observed at the periastron)

limitations_admitted.value: Sample size with measured gas-to-dust size ratios and eccentricities is too small to definitively test a correlation between size ratio and orbital eccentricity.

evidence.loc: Comparison of gas disc radii with tidal truncation models
evidence.quote: However, to definitively refute a dependence of the gas-dust size ratio on the eccentricity, it is necessary to significantly increase the sample of systems with measured size ratio and eccentricity.

referee_caveats_inferred: The maximum recoverable scale of ~1.8'' is smaller than the derived R95,gas of UZ Tau E (2.40'') and comparable to CIDA 9 A (1.70''), meaning extended outer gas emission could be affected by spatial filtering.

Comparing non-parametric image-plane cumulative flux gas radii with parametric/deconvolved uv-plane Galario dust radii mixes two different resolution regimes, and also differs from the parametric Gaussian/Nuker gas profile fitting used in the Lupus comparison sample (Sanchis et al. 2021).

The analytical tidal truncation comparison assumes coplanarity between the discs and the binary orbit, whereas Section 5.3 shows that most of the resolved binaries have significant mutual disc misalignments (25-50 deg).

reproducibility.score_reason: The paper clearly describes the ALMA project codes, calibration strategy, imaging weights, kinematic fitting with eddy/bettermoments, and aperture photometry steps, and tabulates all intermediate and final quantities. Minor low-level imaging/self-calibration parameters and moment-0 integration ranges are not explicitly listed.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: All ALMA datasets are public in the archive, the analysis uses standard open-source tools (CASA, bettermoments, eddy) and straightforward curve-of-growth aperture photometry, and the main deliverables are well-defined numeric tables of disc inclinations, position angles, fluxes, radii, and minimum eccentricities.
